∇ ELECTRODYNAMICS FIELD LAB
Watch & QuestionPython lab

INDEPENDENT TRANSFER / SUBMIT A DESIGN ARGUMENT

One coating, many wavelengths.

Choose a nominal coating thickness for a sensor window of index 2.25. Light arrives at normal incidence from air. The available material has index 1.40 and the measured thickness can deviate by ±8 nm. Illumination spans 450–650 nm.

What to turn in

  1. Derive the ideal matching index and physical thickness at 525 nm.
  2. Choose a nominal thickness for the available film by minimizing worst-case reflectance across both wavelength and thickness tolerance.
  3. Use the numerical boundary solver and the independent reflection formula. Compare to the bare window and report a convergence check.
  4. Plot the reflectance range, label wavelength and power units, and explain how you would measure performance under a relaxed assumption.

Rubric

CriterionEvidence for full credit
Field model (25%)Correct boundary conditions, phasor convention, units, assumptions and ideal match.
Computation (25%)Reproducible minimax search, refinement check and independent calculation at the worst case.
Interpretation (25%)Labelled spectra, distinction between reflectance and amplitude, comparison to bare glass, tolerance stated.
Scientific judgement (25%)A plausible test, a specific failure mode for the model, and a measurable criterion for revising the design.

Bring the reasoning and executable notebook to your instructor or study group. Use the optional practice questions as formative feedback.
